native_mcp_support.notes: Responses API supports remote MCP servers as a first-class tool type. Also available in Realtime API.

skills_concept.value: Skills (Responses API / Codex) + GPTs/Assistants (ChatGPT product) + Agents SDK. Skills are reusable packaged capabilities uploaded and attached to hosted environments; injected via hidden system-prompt stub at runtime. GPTs are the ChatGPT-product analog.
skills_concept.notes: Two distinct systems: (1) Skills in the raw API/Codex — uploadable instruction bundles invoked via tool_triggered mechanism; (2) GPTs/Assistants in the ChatGPT product — always-on per-conversation custom instructions.

context_window_tokens.notes: 1,050,000 token context window per model page. Prompts >272K input tokens billed at 2x input / 1.5x output.

input_output_shared.notes: Single shared pool: 1,050,000 total tokens; max output 128,000, so max input ~922,000.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: 1,050,000 context_window - 128,000 max_output = 922,000. Not explicitly documented as a separate max input figure.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Default max_output not separately documented; model page only lists 128,000 as max output.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: 128,000 max output tokens. Includes reasoning tokens for reasoning-enabled calls.

extended_context.notes: 1,050,000 is the GA production window — no additional beta/extended mode documented.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Model page shows 'Reasoning token support' and completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens is tracked. Reasoning effort parameter supported (none/low/medium/high/xhigh). Reasoning tokens billed as output.

tokenizer_family.notes: GPT-5.x family uses o200k_base, consistent with GPT-4o and later. Confirmed by tiktoken MODEL_TO_ENCODING updates for gpt-5.x strings.

tokenizer_public.notes: tiktoken is open-source (MIT license) and publicly available on PyPI and GitHub.

count_tokens_method.value: import tiktoken; enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model('gpt-5.5'); tokens = enc.encode(text). Alternatively use the Responses API with include=['usage'] before generating output.
count_tokens_method.notes: Responses API token counting endpoint also available: set stream=False, include=['usage'] to get exact counts including tool definitions without estimation.

image_token_rule.value: Low-res: fixed 85 tokens. High-res: 85 base + 170 per 512x512 tile. Input only (image output not supported for gpt-5.5).
image_token_rule.notes: Standard OpenAI image tiling formula; gpt-5.5 accepts image input but produces text output only.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio modality not supported for gpt-5.5 (model page: Audio — Not supported).

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Rough estimate for English prose with o200k_base tokenizer. Use tiktoken for exact counts.

native_mcp.notes: Model page confirms MCP: Supported via Responses API. Remote MCP servers connect as a tool type.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: parallel_tool_calls parameter supported; defaults to true for GPT-5.x models.

max_tools_hard.notes: Assistants API deep-dive page explicitly states 'up to 128 tools' per assistant/request. Error message when exceeded: 'Expected an array with maximum length 128'. Applies to both Assistants API and Chat Completions / Responses API tool arrays. Consistent across GPT-4o and GPT-5 family.

max_tools_practical.notes: Empirical degradation point. Community consensus and Berkeley FCL data suggest accuracy degrades past ~30-50 tools. OpenAI's own tool_search documentation suggests pairing it with large tool surfaces to defer rarely-used tools. Using 40 as practical midpoint.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI function/tool JSON schema format: {type, function: {name, description, parameters, strict}}. Tool definitions injected into prompt and billed as input tokens.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. Responses API token-counting endpoint can return exact counts including tools.

tool_search_deferral.notes: OpenAI Tool Search feature: defer large tool surfaces, group with namespaces, load only relevant functions at runtime. Supported on gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, and gpt-5.4-mini. NOT supported on gpt-5.4-nano.

max_tool_name_len.notes: Function names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ with max 64 characters. API returns 'string_above_max_length' / 'does not conform to required pattern' errors when violated. MCP tool names get namespaced by clients (e.g. 'server_toolname'), consuming chars from this budget. | pattern=^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$

max_tool_description_len.notes: API enforces a 1024-character limit on tool/function description strings. Error: 'Expected a string with maximum length 1024'. Not explicitly stated in official docs page but consistently reported via API error responses. Workaround: move detail into the system prompt.

max_request_size.notes: No published per-request payload size cap for function calling / Responses API found in official docs. Responses API has a 50 MB cap for file inputs. The effective limit is the context window token count (tool defs count as input tokens). No separate byte-limit documented.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Community reports indicate a ~512KB limit on tool output (function result) submitted back to the model. Not explicitly documented in official API reference. Tool output tokens also count against the context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No fixed numeric cap on simultaneous tool calls per turn. parallel_tool_calls is a boolean (true/false) — when true, model may emit multiple tool calls in one turn but there is no documented max count. No numeric limit published.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No API-enforced cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn. The Agents SDK defaults to 20 max_turns as a safety measure, but this is SDK-level, not API-enforced. Agentic loops run until the model returns a final message or context window is exhausted.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented hard cap on the number of remote MCP servers that can be connected. ChatGPT help doc confirms 'multiple first-party and third-party apps in a single prompt' are supported. The binding constraint is the 128-tool aggregate limit per request.

max_total_tools.notes: Same as max_tools_hard: 128 tools total per request regardless of how many MCP servers contribute tools. Tools from multiple connected servers all count toward this single 128-tool budget.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: JSON Schema for parameters follows OpenAI's structured outputs subset. Strict mode (strict:true) enforces: (1) additionalProperties must be false on all objects; (2) all properties must be listed in 'required'; (3) max 100 object properties total; (4) max 5 nesting levels; (5) anyOf supported only for nullable types (anyOf: [{type: X}, {type: null}]); (6) $ref not supported in strict mode; (7) oneOf/allOf have problems in strict mode; (8) keywords pattern, minLength, minimum, format are accepted but NOT enforced by the model. Non-strict mode accepts a broader subset. No documented byte-size limit on total tool definition payload beyond the context window.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP (Responses API): tool definitions from MCP servers are fetched at request time, cached with the request, and billed as input tokens. allowed_tools parameter can filter which tools are exposed from a connected MCP server to reduce token overhead. ChatGPT MCP apps (Business/Enterprise): full MCP with write actions available in beta; no hard server-count cap documented but tools must fit within 128-tool budget. Deep research (ChatGPT product): MCP servers limited to read/fetch actions only. Rate limits: per-model RPM/TPM limits apply (see platform.openai.com/settings/limits); no tool-specific rate limits documented separately.

strict_function_schema.notes: OpenAI strict mode (strict:true): enforces additionalProperties:false, all-required, max 100 properties, max 5 nesting, bans oneOf/$ref.

skills_supported.notes: Skills are uploadable instruction bundles (files) attachable to hosted environments via Responses API. Model page confirms Skills: Supported.

skills_loading_model.notes: Service adds each skill's name, description, and path to the hidden system-prompt context so the model knows the skill exists; actual skill content is fetched/executed when the model triggers it. Not always-on full injection.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Each skill's stub (name + description + path) is injected into the hidden system prompt and billed as input tokens. Full skill instructions are loaded on demand when model triggers the skill. Per the docs: 'Skill instructions are user prompt input (not system prompt input)' when executed.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: Responses API has a hidden system-prompt prefix for enabled tools (MCP stubs, skill stubs). Exact token count not published; use the Responses API token-counting endpoint (include=['usage'], stream=False) to measure overhead per configuration.

prompt_caching.notes: Automatic prompt caching enabled for all prompts >=1024 tokens. gpt-5.5 uses Extended Prompt Cache Retention (24h default) — in-memory is NOT supported for gpt-5.5. Tool definitions and system prompts are cacheable as static prefix. Cached input priced at $0.50/1M tokens (90% discount from standard $5.00/1M).

memory_feature.notes: No persistent memory in the raw API for gpt-5.5. Memory is a ChatGPT product feature (not the API). Codex has 'Memories' via Chronicle but that is the Codex product, not raw API. Developers can implement memory via external storage + retrieval.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard processing, context <272K tokens. Prompts >272K: billed at 2x input for the full session.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard processing. Prompts >272K: output billed at 1.5x output for the full session. Reasoning tokens billed as output.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: 90% discount from standard input price. Extended cache retention (24h) is default for gpt-5.5.

batch_discount.notes: Batch API: 24-hour async processing at 50% discount on both input and output tokens.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image inputs billed at standard text token rates using tile-based formula: 85 base tokens + 170 per 512x512 tile (high-res). Audio: not supported for this model.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens is part of completion_tokens (output). Reasoning effort supports: none/low/medium (default)/high/xhigh.

models.notes: GPT-5.5 is OpenAI's newest frontier model (GA April 24, 2026). Snapshot: gpt-5.5-2026-04-23. Default prompt cache retention is 24h (extended); in-memory cache not supported. Context surcharge kicks in at >272K input tokens.
